title: The Night Watch
subject: English
source: Written for english/y5 lesson 18 (Teacher's short story: The Night Watch (a girl and her grandfather at a rooftop telescope; written for this lesson))
intro: Lesson 18. Read the story, then answer the inference questions with evidence (VIPERS).

passage.title: The Night Watch
paras: The roof was Grandad's favourite place. Up there, above the car park and the chip shop and the sleeping school, the sky was bigger than anywhere else in town. Maryam pulled her coat tight and climbed the last few rungs of the ladder.
"You came," Grandad said, without turning round. He was bent over the old brass telescope, the one he never let anyone touch. "Good. Tonight is the night."
He only smiled and tapped the side of his nose. The wind tugged at the plastic sheet that covered the water tank. Somewhere below, a dog barked twice and stopped.

For a long time nothing happened. Maryam's fingers went numb. The stars looked exactly like they always did: small, cold and far away. She was about to say she wanted to go in when Grandad's hand closed gently on her arm.

She put her eye to the cold rim of the telescope. At first there was only darkness. Then, in the middle of it, a tiny streak of light slid across the black like a match being struck very carefully. Another followed it. Then three more, all at once.
Maryam forgot her fingers. She forgot the wind and the dog and the ladder. She held her breath so that she would not shake the telescope.
"Every year," Grandad said quietly, "I wait for this. Your grandmother used to wait with me." His voice caught, just for a moment. "Subhan Allah. Look how He lights the sky."
Maryam did not take her eye from the lens, but she reached out and found his hand. It was colder than hers. She held it anyway, all through the shower of light, until the sky was quiet again.

questions.q: How do we know the telescope matters to Grandad?
questions.a: It is the one he 'never let anyone touch'; he is bent over it before she arrives.

questions.q: Why do you think Grandad says 'Tonight is the night' but will not explain?
questions.a: He wants it to be a surprise; he tapped his nose to keep the secret, which builds suspense.

questions.q: Find two details that build tension while they wait.
questions.a: Any two: the wind tugging the sheet; the dog barking twice and stopping; 'for a long time nothing happened'; numb fingers.

questions.q: What do you think Maryam sees? Give evidence.
questions.a: Shooting stars (a meteor shower): 'a tiny streak of light slid across the black', 'more, all at once', 'the shower of light'.

questions.q: Why does Grandad's voice 'catch'? What does Maryam do, and what does it show about her?
questions.a: He is remembering his wife who has died; Maryam holds his hand, which shows she understands and is kind.
